main_diagnosis: The simulator is missing one or more ion channel(s) that modulate subthreshold and adaptation dynamics. The high neg_avg_log_marginal_NLE (~26.5) indicates the model cannot match experimental voltage traces, most likely because a slow K+ adaptation current (M-current, I_M) is absent. The parameters gbar_X1, param_i, and param_j are available but unused in channel kinetics, tau_V_inv, and V_inf computations.

issues.description: Missing M-current (slow muscarinic K+ channel) gating variable and kinetics. Without I_M, the model cannot reproduce spike-frequency adaptation or correct subthreshold oscillations. The relevant unused parameters are gbar_X1 (conductance), param_i (half-activation voltage offset), and param_j (time constant scaling).
issues.location: All '# BEGIN EDITABLE SECTION' blocks: kinetics definition, state variable declaration, initialization, loop body (alpha/beta computation, tau_V_inv, V_inf, state update)

issues.description: gbar_X2 and the second channel slot are currently not used. Since the instructions say to keep the model simple and only add one channel if necessary, verify after adding I_M whether gbar_X2 is still needed. Leaving it unused wastes a degree of freedom and may confuse parameter inference.

issues.suggestion: After adding the M-current and re-evaluating metrics, if the neg_avg_log_marginal_NLE drops significantly, do not add a second channel (gbar_X2). If residual discrepancy persists, consider adding an h-current (HCN, hyperpolarization-activated) using gbar_X2 with a negative reversal potential near param_i, as it affects pacemaking and rebound bursting. Only add it if performance metrics justify the added complexity.
